void register_isampleselector()
{
    // ISampleSelector
    //
    scope ss =
         class_<Abc::ISampleSelector>(
             "ISampleSelector",
             "The ISampleSelector utilize the selection of the sample index "
             "for the initialized requested index or time",
             init<AbcA::index_t>(
                 ( arg( "requestedIndex" ) ),
                 "Create an ISampleSelector with the given requested index") )
        .def( init<AbcA::chrono_t,
              optional<Abc::ISampleSelector::TimeIndexType> >(
                  ( arg( "requestedTime" ),
                    arg( "requestedIndexType ") ),
                  "Create an ISampleSelector with the given requested time and "
                  " the optional request index type" ) )
        .def( init<>(
                  "Create an ISampleSelector with the requested index value of "
                  "0 and the requested index type of kNearIndex" ) )
        .def( "getIndex",
              &Abc::ISampleSelector::getIndex,
              ( arg( "timeSampling" ), arg( "numSamples" ) ),
              "Return the requested index with the given time sampling and "
              "the number of samples" )
        .def( "getRequestedIndex",
              &Abc::ISampleSelector::getRequestedIndex,
              "Return the requested Index" )
        .def( "getRequestedTime",
              &Abc::ISampleSelector::getRequestedTime,
              "Return the requested time" )
        .def( "getRequestedTimeIndexType",
              &Abc::ISampleSelector::getRequestedTimeIndexType,
              "Return the requested time index type" )
        ;
    // Implicit conversions for ISampleSelector
    //
    implicitly_convertible<AbcA::index_t, Abc::ISampleSelector>();
    implicitly_convertible<AbcA::chrono_t, Abc::ISampleSelector>();
   
    // TimeIndexType
    //
    enum_<Abc::ISampleSelector::TimeIndexType>( "TimeIndexType" )
        .value( "kFloorIndex", Abc::ISampleSelector::kFloorIndex )
        .value( "kCeilIndex", Abc::ISampleSelector::kCeilIndex )
        .value( "kNearIndex", Abc::ISampleSelector::kNearIndex )
        ;
}

void register_cmath(py::module& m) {
    // CMathFunction enum
    py::enum_<sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction>(m, "CMathFunction")
        // Trigonometric functions
        .value("sin", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::sin)
        .value("cos", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::cos)
        .value("tan", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::tan)
        .value("asin", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::asin)
        .value("acos", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::acos)
        .value("atan", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::atan)
        .value("atan2", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::atan2)
        // Hyperbolic functions
        .value("sinh", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::sinh)
        .value("cosh", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::cosh)
        .value("tanh", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::tanh)
        .value("asinh", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::asinh)
        .value("acosh", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::acosh)
        .value("atanh", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::atanh)
        // Exponential and logarithmic functions
        .value("exp", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::exp)
        .value("exp2", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::exp2)
        .value("exp10", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::exp10)
        .value("expm1", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::expm1)
        .value("log", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::log)
        .value("log10", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::log10)
        .value("log2", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::log2)
        .value("log1p", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::log1p)
        // Power functions
        .value("pow", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::pow)
        .value("sqrt", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::sqrt)
        .value("cbrt", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::cbrt)
        .value("hypot", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::hypot)
        // Error and gamma functions
        .value("erf", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::erf)
        .value("erfc", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::erfc)
        .value("tgamma", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::tgamma)
        .value("lgamma", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::lgamma)
        // Rounding and remainder functions
        .value("fabs", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::fabs)
        .value("ceil", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::ceil)
        .value("floor", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::floor)
        .value("trunc", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::trunc)
        .value("round", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::round)
        .value("lround", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::lround)
        .value("llround", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::llround)
        .value("roundeven", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::roundeven)
        .value("nearbyint", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::nearbyint)
        .value("rint", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::rint)
        .value("lrint", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::lrint)
        .value("llrint", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::llrint)
        .value("fmod", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::fmod)
        .value("remainder", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::remainder)
        // Floating-point manipulation functions

int main(){
    set<int> s; // set of integers
    s.insert(1); // insert 1 into the set
    s.insert(2); // insert 2 into the set
    s.insert(3); // insert 3 into the set
    s.insert(4); // insert 4 into the set
    s.insert(6); // insert 6 into the set
    s.insert(1); // insert 1 into the set again (duplicate, will not be added)
    s.insert(2); // insert 2 into the set again (duplicate, will not be added)
    for(auto i: s){ // iterate over the set
        cout<<i<<" "; // print each element in the set
    }
    cout<<endl; // print a newline
    cout<<s.size()<<endl; // print size of the set (4)
    cout<<s.max_size()<<endl; // print max size of the set (depends on the system)
    cout<<s.empty()<<endl; // print whether the set is empty or not (0 for false, 1 for true)
    cout<<s.count(1)<<endl; // print count of element 1 in the set (1 if exists, 0 if not)
    cout<<*(s.lower_bound(4))<<endl; // print the first element that is greater than or equal to 4 (4)
    cout<<*(s.lower_bound(5))<<endl; // print the first element that is greater than or equal to 5 (6)
    cout<<*(s.lower_bound(7))<<endl; // 0
    cout<<*(s.upper_bound(4))<<endl; // print the first element that is greater than 4 (6)
    cout<<*(s.upper_bound(5))<<endl; // print the first element that is greater than 5 (6)
    
    return 0;
}

namespace py = pybind11;
using namespace torch::comms::fr;
PYBIND11_MODULE(_fr, m) {
  // Bind FlightRecorderHook class
  py::class_<FlightRecorderHook, std::shared_ptr<FlightRecorderHook>>(
      m,
      "FlightRecorderHook",
      R"(
FlightRecorderHook tracks all collective operations in flight for TorchComm communicators.
The output format matches the OSS FlightRecorder format from PyTorch's
distributed module, so traces can be analyzed using the same fr_trace
analysis tools.
Example:
    >>> from torchcomms.hooks import fr
    >>> comm = torchcomms.new_comm("nccl", device, "world")
    >>> recorder = fr.FlightRecorderHook(max_entries=1024)
    >>> recorder.register_with_comm(comm)
    >>> # ... run some collectives ...
    >>> json_trace = recorder.dump_json()
For testing, use ``isolated=True`` to create a separate FlightRecorder instance
that is not shared with other hooks::
    >>> recorder = fr.FlightRecorderHook(max_entries=100, isolated=True)
      )")
      .def(
          py::init<size_t, bool>(),
          R"(
          Create a FlightRecorderHook with specified buffer size.
          Args:
              max_entries: Maximum number of entries in the ring buffer.
                          Older entries are overwritten when full.
              isolated: If True, creates an isolated FlightRecorder instance
                       for this hook instead of using the global singleton.
          )",
          py::arg("max_entries") = 2048,
          py::arg("isolated") = false)
      .def(
          "register_with_comm",
          &FlightRecorderHook::registerWithComm,
          R"(
          Register this hook with a TorchComm communicator.
          Args:
              comm: The communicator to register with.
          )",
          py::arg("comm"),
          py::call_guard<py::gil_scoped_release>())
      .def(
          "unregister",
          &FlightRecorderHook::unregister,
          "Unregister this hook from all communicators.",
          py::call_guard<py::gil_scoped_release>())
      .def(
          "dump_json",
          &FlightRecorderHook::dump_json,
          R"(
          Dump all entries as a JSON string in the OSS FlightRecorder format.
          This format is compatible with the fr_trace analyzer tools from
          torch.distributed.flight_recorder.
          Args:
              include_completed: If False, only return entries that are not completed.
          Returns:
              A JSON string containing the flight recorder trace.
          )",
          py::arg("include_completed") = true,
          py::call_guard<py::gil_scoped_release>())
      .def(
          "reset",
          &FlightRecorderHook::reset,
          "Clear all entries and reset sequence counters.",
          py::call_guard<py::gil_scoped_release>())
      .def(
          "is_enabled",
          &FlightRecorderHook::isEnabled,
          "Check if the hook has registered communicators.")
      .def(
          "__len__",
          &FlightRecorderHook::size,
          "Get the current number of entries.")
      .def(
          "size",
          &FlightRecorderHook::size,
          "Get the current number of entries.")
      .def(
          "dump_file",
          &FlightRecorderHook::dump_file,
          R"(
          Dump the flight recorder trace and write it to a file.
          The output location is controlled by the TORCHCOMM_FR_DUMP_TEMP_FILE
          environment variable. Files are written as <prefix><rank>.
          Args:
              rank: The rank to use for the file name.
              include_completed: If False, only dump entries that are not completed.
          )",
          py::arg("rank"),
          py::arg("include_completed") = true,
          py::call_guard<py::gil_scoped_release>());
}

//-*****************************************************************************
void register_filmbackxformop()
{
    // FilmBackXformOp
    //
    class_<AbcG::FilmBackXformOp>(
          "FilmBackXformOp",
          "This class holds the data about a particular transform operation, but does "
          "not hold the actual data to calculate a 3x3 matrix.  It holds the type of "
          "operation (Translate, Scale, Matrix), a hint about the type which "
          "can be interpreted by packages like Maya, and what particular parts of the "
          "operations can change over time.",
         init<const AbcG::FilmBackXformOperationType, const std::string&>(
             ( arg( "type" ), arg( "hint" ) = 0 ),
             "Create an FilmBackXformOp with default settings based on the type of operation "
             "and a hint about the type for applications like Maya." ) )
        .def( init<>("Create an empty FilmBackXformOp" ) )
        .def( "getType",
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getType,
              "Get the type of transform operation. (Translate, Scale, "
              "Matrix)")
        .def( "getHint",
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getHint,
              "Get the Hint to help "
              "disambiguate certain options that may have the same type.")
        .def( "getTypeHint",
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getHint,
              "Get the type and hint, where the first character is the type"
              "(t for translate, s for scale, m for matrix) and the rest of the"
              "returned string is the optional hint value." )
        .def( "getNumChannels",
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getNumChannels,
              "Get the number of components that this operation has based on the type. "
              "Translate and Scale have 2 and Matrix has 9." )
        .def( "getChannelValue", 
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getChannelValue,
              ( arg( "index" ) ),
              "Get a single channel, 0 will be returned if iIndex is greater than"
              "numChannels - 1" )
        .def( "setChannelValue",
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::setChannelValue,
              ( arg( "index" ), arg( "value" ) ),
              "Set a single channel; nothing will be set if iIndex is greater than"
              "numchannels - 1.")
        .def( "setTranslate", 
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::setTranslate,
              ( arg( "trans" ) ) )
        .def( "setScale", 
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::setScale,
              ( arg( "scale" ) ) )
        .def( "setMatrix", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::setMatrix,
              ( arg( "matrix" ) ) )
        .def( "getTranslate", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getTranslate )
        .def( "getScale", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getScale )
        .def( "getMatrix", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getMatrix )
        .def( "isTranslateOp", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::isTranslateOp )
        .def( "isScaleOp", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::isScaleOp )
        .def( "isMatrixOp", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::isMatrixOp )
        ;
}

// Checks if type T is convertible to any integer type (excluding char and bool types)
template <typename T>
struct is_convertible_to_int 
    : boost::mpl::and_<
          boost::mpl::not_<std::is_same<T, bool>>,
          boost::mpl::not_<std::is_same<T, char>>,
          boost::mpl::not_<std::is_same<T, unsigned char>>,
          boost::mpl::not_<std::is_same<T, signed char>>,
          boost::mpl::not_<std::is_same<T, wchar_t>>,
          boost::mpl::not_<std::is_same<T, char16_t>>,
          boost::mpl::not_<std::is_same<T, char32_t>>,
          boost::mpl::or_<
              boost::is_convertible<T, int>,
              boost::is_convertible<T, unsigned int>,
              boost::is_convertible<T, long>,
              boost::is_convertible<T, unsigned long>,
              boost::is_convertible<T, long long>,
              boost::is_convertible<T, unsigned long long>
          >
      > {};

        "bool?    pack_gqa,"

        "Tensor?  sinks"

//-*****************************************************************************
void register_isampleselector()
{
    // ISampleSelector
    //
    scope ss =
         class_<Abc::ISampleSelector>(
             "ISampleSelector",
             "The ISampleSelector utilize the selection of the sample index "
             "for the initialized requested index or time",
             init<AbcA::index_t>(
                 ( arg( "requestedIndex" ) ),
                 "Create an ISampleSelector with the given requested index") )
        .def( init<AbcA::chrono_t,
              optional<Abc::ISampleSelector::TimeIndexType> >(
                  ( arg( "requestedTime" ),
                    arg( "requestedIndexType ") ),
                  "Create an ISampleSelector with the given requested time and "
                  " the optional request index type" ) )
        .def( init<>(
                  "Create an ISampleSelector with the requested index value of "
                  "0 and the requested index type of kNearIndex" ) )
        .def( "getIndex",
              &Abc::ISampleSelector::getIndex,
              ( arg( "timeSampling" ), arg( "numSamples" ) ),
              "Return the requested index with the given time sampling and "
              "the number of samples" )
        .def( "getRequestedIndex",
              &Abc::ISampleSelector::getRequestedIndex,
              "Return the requested Index" )
        .def( "getRequestedTime",
              &Abc::ISampleSelector::getRequestedTime,
              "Return the requested time" )
        .def( "getRequestedTimeIndexType",
              &Abc::ISampleSelector::getRequestedTimeIndexType,
              "Return the requested time index type" )
        ;

    // Implicit conversions for ISampleSelector
    //
    implicitly_convertible<AbcA::index_t, Abc::ISampleSelector>();
    implicitly_convertible<AbcA::chrono_t, Abc::ISampleSelector>();

    // TimeIndexType
    //
    enum_<Abc::ISampleSelector::TimeIndexType>( "TimeIndexType" )
        .value( "kFloorIndex", Abc::ISampleSelector::kFloorIndex )
        .value( "kCeilIndex", Abc::ISampleSelector::kCeilIndex )
        .value( "kNearIndex", Abc::ISampleSelector::kNearIndex )
        ;
}

// Register CMathFunction enum to Python
void register_cmath(py::module& m)
{
    // CMathFunction enum
    py::enum_<sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction>(m, "CMathFunction")
        // Trigonometric functions
        .value("sin", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::sin)
        .value("cos", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::cos)
        .value("tan", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::tan)
        .value("asin", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::asin)
        .value("acos", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::acos)
        .value("atan", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::atan)
        .value("atan2", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::atan2)
        // Hyperbolic functions
        .value("sinh", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::sinh)
        .value("cosh", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::cosh)
        .value("tanh", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::tanh)
        .value("asinh", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::asinh)
        .value("acosh", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::acosh)
        .value("atanh", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::atanh)
        // Exponential and logarithmic functions
        .value("exp", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::exp)
        .value("exp2", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::exp2)
        .value("exp10", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::exp10)
        .value("expm1", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::expm1)
        .value("log", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::log)
        .value("log10", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::log10)
        .value("log2", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::log2)
        .value("log1p", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::log1p)
        // Power functions
        .value("pow", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::pow)
        .value("sqrt", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::sqrt)
        .value("cbrt", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::cbrt)
        .value("hypot", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::hypot)
        // Error and gamma functions
        .value("erf", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::erf)
        .value("erfc", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::erfc)
        .value("tgamma", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::tgamma)
        .value("lgamma", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::lgamma)
        // Rounding and remainder functions
        .value("fabs", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::fabs)
        .value("ceil", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::ceil)
        .value("floor", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::floor)
        .value("trunc", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::trunc)
        .value("round", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::round)
        .value("lround", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::lround)
        .value("llround", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::llround)
        .value("roundeven", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::roundeven)
        .value("nearbyint", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::nearbyint)
        .value("rint", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::rint)
        .value("lrint", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::lrint)
        .value("llrint", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::llrint)
        .value("fmod", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::fmod)
        .value("remainder", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::remainder)
        // Floating-point manipulation functions
        .value("frexp", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::frexp)
        .value("ldexp", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::ldexp)
        .value("modf", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::modf)
        .value("scalbn", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::scalbn)
        .value("scalbln", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::scalbln)
        .value("ilogb", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::ilogb)
        .value("logb", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::logb)
        .value("nextafter", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::nextafter)
        .value("nexttoward", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::nexttoward)
        .value("copysign", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::copysign)
        // Minimum, maximum, difference functions
        .value("fmax", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::fmax)
        .value("fmin", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::fmin)
        .value("fdim", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::fdim)
        // Other functions
        .value("fma", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::fma)
        .export_values();
}

// FlightRecorderHook Python bindings
PYBIND11_MODULE(_fr, m)
{
    // Bind FlightRecorderHook class
    py::class_<FlightRecorderHook, std::shared_ptr<FlightRecorderHook>>(
        m,
        "FlightRecorderHook",
        R"(
FlightRecorderHook tracks all collective operations in flight for TorchComm communicators.
The output format matches the OSS FlightRecorder format from PyTorch's
distributed module, so traces can be analyzed using the same fr_trace
analysis tools.

Example:
    >>> from torchcomms.hooks import fr
    >>> comm = torchcomms.new_comm("nccl", device, "world")
    >>> recorder = fr.FlightRecorderHook(max_entries=1024)
    >>> recorder.register_with_comm(comm)
    >>> # ... run some collectives ...
    >>> json_trace = recorder.dump_json()

For testing, use ``isolated=True`` to create a separate FlightRecorder instance
that is not shared with other hooks::

    >>> recorder = fr.FlightRecorderHook(max_entries=100, isolated=True)
      )")
        .def(
            py::init<size_t, bool>(),
            R"(
          Create a FlightRecorderHook with specified buffer size.

          Args:
              max_entries: Maximum number of entries in the ring buffer.
                          Older entries are overwritten when full.
              isolated: If True, creates an isolated FlightRecorder instance
                       for this hook instead of using the global singleton.
          )",
            py::arg("max_entries") = 2048,
            py::arg("isolated") = false)
        .def(
            "register_with_comm",
            &FlightRecorderHook::registerWithComm,
            R"(
          Register this hook with a TorchComm communicator.

          Args:
              comm: The communicator to register with.
          )",
            py::arg("comm"),
            py::call_guard<py::gil_scoped_release>())
        .def(
            "unregister",
            &FlightRecorderHook::unregister,
            "Unregister this hook from all communicators.",
            py::call_guard<py::gil_scoped_release>())
        .def(
            "dump_json",
            &FlightRecorderHook::dump_json,
            R"(
          Dump all entries as a JSON string in the OSS FlightRecorder format.
          This format is compatible with the fr_trace analyzer tools from
          torch.distributed.flight_recorder.

          Args:
              include_completed: If False, only return entries that are not completed.

          Returns:
              A JSON string containing the flight recorder trace.
          )",
            py::arg("include_completed") = true,
            py::call_guard<py::gil_scoped_release>())
        .def(
            "reset",
            &FlightRecorderHook::reset,
            "Clear all entries and reset sequence counters.",
            py::call_guard<py::gil_scoped_release>())
        .def(
            "is_enabled",
            &FlightRecorderHook::isEnabled,
            "Check if the hook has registered communicators.")
        .def(
            "__len__",
            &FlightRecorderHook::size,
            "Get the current number of entries.")
        .def(
            "size",
            &FlightRecorderHook::size,
            "Get the current number of entries.")
        .def(
            "dump_file",
            &FlightRecorderHook::dump_file,
            R"(
          Dump the flight recorder trace and write it to a file.
          The output location is controlled by the TORCHCOMM_FR_DUMP_TEMP_FILE
          environment variable. Files are written as <prefix><rank>.

          Args:
              rank: The rank to use for the file name.
              include_completed: If False, only dump entries that are not completed.
          )",
            py::arg("rank"),
            py::arg("include_completed") = true,
            py::call_guard<py::gil_scoped_release>());
}

//-*****************************************************************************
void register_filmbackxformop()
{
    // FilmBackXformOp registration
    //
    class_<AbcG::FilmBackXformOp>(
          "FilmBackXformOp",
          "This class holds the data about a particular transform operation, but does "
          "not hold the actual data to calculate a 3x3 matrix.  It holds the type of "
          "operation (Translate, Scale, Matrix), a hint about the type which "
          "can be interpreted by packages like Maya, and what particular parts of the "
          "operations can change over time.",
         init<const AbcG::FilmBackXformOperationType, const std::string&>(
             ( arg( "type" ), arg( "hint" ) = 0 ),
             "Create an FilmBackXformOp with default settings based on the type of operation "
             "and a hint about the type for applications like Maya." ) )
        .def( init<>( "Create an empty FilmBackXformOp" ) )
        .def( "getType",
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getType,
              "Get the type of transform operation. (Translate, Scale, "
              "Matrix)")
        .def( "getHint",
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getHint,
              "Get the Hint to help "
              "disambiguate certain options that may have the same type.")
        .def( "getTypeHint",
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getHint,
              "Get the type and hint, where the first character is the type"
              "(t for translate, s for scale, m for matrix) and the rest of the"
              "returned string is the optional hint value." )
        .def( "getNumChannels",
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getNumChannels,
              "Get the number of components that this operation has based on the type. "
              "Translate and Scale have 2 and Matrix has 9." )
        .def( "getChannelValue", 
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getChannelValue,
              ( arg( "index" ) ),
              "Get a single channel, 0 will be returned if iIndex is greater than"
              "numChannels - 1" )
        .def( "setChannelValue",
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::setChannelValue,
              ( arg( "index" ), arg( "value" ) ),
              "Set a single channel; nothing will be set if iIndex is greater than"
              "numchannels - 1.")
        .def( "setTranslate", 
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::setTranslate,
              ( arg( "trans" ) ) )
        .def( "setScale", 
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::setScale,
              ( arg( "scale" ) ) )
        .def( "setMatrix", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::setMatrix,
              ( arg( "matrix" ) ) )
        .def( "getTranslate", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getTranslate )
        .def( "getScale", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getScale )
        .def( "getMatrix", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getMatrix )
        .def( "isTranslateOp", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::isTranslateOp )
        .def( "isScaleOp", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::isScaleOp )
        .def( "isMatrixOp", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::isMatrixOp )
        ;
}

// Check if type T is convertible to any integer type, excluding character and boolean types
template <typename T>
struct is_integer_convertible : boost::mpl::and_<
    boost::mpl::not_<std::is_same<T, bool>>,
    boost::mpl::not_<std::is_same<T, char>>,
    boost::mpl::not_<std::is_same<T, unsigned char>>,
    boost::mpl::not_<std::is_same<T, signed char>>,
    boost::mpl::not_<std::is_same<T, wchar_t>>,
    boost::mpl::not_<std::is_same<T, char16_t>>,
    boost::mpl::not_<std::is_same<T, char32_t>>,
    boost::mpl::or_<
        boost::is_convertible<T, int>,
        boost::is_convertible<T, unsigned int>,
        boost::is_convertible<T, long>,
        boost::is_convertible<T, unsigned long>,
        boost::is_convertible<T, long long>,
        boost::is_convertible<T, unsigned long long>
    >
> {};

 *        Gathers counter data from dispatch packets and stores them
 *        in the specified buffer_id. The buffer may aggregate data
 *        from multiple dispatches (identified by correlation id).
 *        Triggers the provided callback according to buffer configuration.
 *
 * @param [in] ctx_id context identifier
 * @param [in] buf_id buffer identifier for storing counting data
 * @param [in] profile_cfg profile configuration for dispatch
 * @return ::rocprofiler_status_t
 */
rocprofiler_status_t
rocprofiler_configure_buffer_dispatch_counting_service(
    rocprofiler_context_id_t                   ctx_id,
    rocprofiler_buffer_id_t                    buf_id,
    rocprofiler_dispatch_counting_service_cb_t cb_func,
    void*                                      cb_func_args)
{
    return rocprofiler::counters::configure_buffered_dispatch(
        ctx_id, buf_id, cb_func, cb_func_args);
}

/**
 * @brief Setup callback-based dispatch profiling for Counting Service.
 *        Collects counter data per dispatch and invokes a callback
 *        immediately upon dispatch completion.
 *
 * @param [in] ctx_id context identifier
 * @param [in] on_dispatch_cb callback invoked when dispatch starts
 * @param [in] on_dispatch_cb_args user data passed to dispatch callback
 * @param [in] on_record_cb callback invoked when profiling data is ready
 * @param [in] on_record_cb_args user data passed to record callback
 * @return ::rocprofiler_status_t
 */
rocprofiler_status_t
rocprofiler_configure_callback_dispatch_counting_service(
    rocprofiler_context_id_t                   ctx_id,
    rocprofiler_dispatch_counting_service_cb_t on_dispatch_cb,
    void*                                      on_dispatch_cb_args,
    rocprofiler_dispatch_counting_record_cb_t  on_record_cb,
    void*                                      on_record_cb_args)
{
    return rocprofiler::counters::configure_callback_dispatch(
        ctx_id, on_dispatch_cb, on_dispatch_cb_args,
        on_record_cb, on_record_cb_args);
}

//-*****************************************************************************
void register_sample_selector()
{
    // ISampleSelector registration
    //
    scope selectorScope =
         class_<Abc::ISampleSelector>(
             "ISampleSelector",
             "The ISampleSelector is used for selecting the sample index "
             "based on the provided index or time parameter",
             init<AbcA::index_t>(
                 ( arg( "sampleIndex" ) ),
                 "Construct an ISampleSelector with a specific sample index") )
        .def( init<AbcA::chrono_t,
              optional<Abc::ISampleSelector::TimeIndexType> >(
                  ( arg( "timeValue" ),
                    arg( "indexMode ") ),
                  "Construct an ISampleSelector using a time value and "
                  "an optional time index mode" ) )
        .def( init<>(
                  "Construct an ISampleSelector with default values: "
                  "index 0 and kNearIndex mode" ) )
        .def( "resolveIndex",
              &Abc::ISampleSelector::getIndex,
              ( arg( "sampling" ), arg( "totalSamples" ) ),
              "Compute and return the actual sample index given the time sampling "
              "and total number of available samples" )
        .def( "requestedIndex",
              &Abc::ISampleSelector::getRequestedIndex,
              "Return the originally requested index value" )
        .def( "requestedTime",
              &Abc::ISampleSelector::getRequestedTime,
              "Return the originally requested time value" )
        .def( "requestedMode",
              &Abc::ISampleSelector::getRequestedTimeIndexType,
              "Return the requested time index mode" )
        ;
    
    // Enable automatic conversion from index and time types to ISampleSelector
    //
    implicitly_convertible<AbcA::index_t, Abc::ISampleSelector>();
    implicitly_convertible<AbcA::chrono_t, Abc::ISampleSelector>();
   
    // TimeIndexType enumeration
    //
    enum_<Abc::ISampleSelector::TimeIndexType>( "TimeIndexType" )
        .value( "kFloorIndex", Abc::ISampleSelector::kFloorIndex )
        .value( "kCeilIndex", Abc::ISampleSelector::kCeilIndex )
        .value( "kNearIndex", Abc::ISampleSelector::kNearIndex )

void register_cmath(py::module& module) {
    // CMathFunction enumeration binding
    py::enum_<sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction>(module, "CMathFunction")
        // Trigonometric operations
        .value("sin", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::sin)
        .value("cos", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::cos)
        .value("tan", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::tan)
        .value("asin", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::asin)
        .value("acos", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::acos)
        .value("atan", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::atan)
        .value("atan2", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::atan2)
        // Hyperbolic operations
        .value("sinh", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::sinh)
        .value("cosh", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::cosh)
        .value("tanh", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::tanh)
        .value("asinh", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::asinh)
        .value("acosh", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::acosh)
        .value("atanh", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::atanh)
        // Exponential and logarithmic operations
        .value("exp", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::exp)
        .value("exp2", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::exp2)
        .value("exp10", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::exp10)
        .value("expm1", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::expm1)
        .value("log", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::log)
        .value("log10", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::log10)
        .value("log2", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::log2)
        .value("log1p", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::log1p)
        // Power operations
        .value("pow", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::pow)
        .value("sqrt", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::sqrt)
        .value("cbrt", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::cbrt)
        .value("hypot", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::hypot)
        // Error and gamma functions
        .value("erf", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::erf)
        .value("erfc", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::erfc)
        .value("tgamma", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::tgamma)

        .value("floor", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::floor)

        .value("round", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::round)
        .value("lround", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::lround)
        .value("llround", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::llround)
        .value("roundeven", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::roundeven)
        .value("nearbyint", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::nearbyint)
        .value("rint", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::rint)
        .value("lrint", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::lrint)
        .value("llrint", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::llrint)
        .value("fmod", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::fmod)
        .value("remainder", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::remainder)
        // Floating-point manipulation operations
        .value("frexp", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::frexp)
        .value("ldexp", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::ldexp)

        .value("scalbn", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::scalbn)
        .value("scalbln", sdfg::math::cmath::CMathFunction::scalbln)

#include <iostream>
#include <set>
using namespace std;

int main() {
    set<int> numbers; // collection of unique integers
    numbers.insert(1); // add 1 to the set
    numbers.insert(2); // add 2 to the set
    numbers.insert(3); // add 3 to the set
    numbers.insert(4); // add 4 to the set
    numbers.insert(6); // add 6 to the set
    numbers.insert(1); // attempt to add 1 again (ignored due to uniqueness)
    numbers.insert(2); // attempt to add 2 again (ignored due to uniqueness)
    
    for(auto element : numbers) { // traverse each element in sorted order
        cout << element << " "; // output current element followed by space
    }
    cout << endl; // end current line
    
    cout << numbers.size() << endl; // display number of distinct elements (4)
    cout << numbers.max_size() << endl; // show maximum possible capacity (platform-dependent)
    cout << numbers.empty() << endl; // indicate if container is empty (0 = not empty)
    cout << numbers.count(1) << endl; // check presence of value 1 (returns 1 if found)
    cout << *(numbers.lower_bound(4)) << endl; // first element >= 4 (outputs 4)
    cout << *(numbers.lower_bound(5)) << endl; // first element >= 5 (outputs 6)
    cout << *(numbers.lower_bound(7)) << endl; // first element >= 7 (outputs 0 if not found, but undefined behavior here)
    cout << *(numbers.upper_bound(4)) << endl; // first element > 4 (outputs 6)
    cout << *(numbers.upper_bound(5)) << endl; // first element > 5 (outputs 6)
    
    return 0;
}

PYBIND11_MODULE(_fr, m) {
  // Bind FlightRecorderHook class
  py::class_<FlightRecorderHook, std::shared_ptr<FlightRecorderHook>>(
      m,
      "FlightRecorderHook",
      R"(
FlightRecorderHook monitors all collective operations in flight for TorchComm communicators.
The output format aligns with the OSS FlightRecorder format from PyTorch's
distributed module, enabling trace analysis using the same fr_trace tools.
Example:
    >>> from torchcomms.hooks import fr
    >>> comm = torchcomms.new_comm("nccl", device, "world")
    >>> monitor = fr.FlightRecorderHook(max_entries=1024)
    >>> monitor.register_with_comm(comm)
    >>> # ... execute some collectives ...
    >>> json_output = monitor.dump_json()
For testing purposes, set ``isolated=True`` to instantiate a dedicated FlightRecorder instance
that remains independent from other hooks::
    >>> monitor = fr.FlightRecorderHook(max_entries=100, isolated=True)
      )")
      .def(
          py::init<size_t, bool>(),
          R"(
          Initialize a FlightRecorderHook with configurable buffer capacity.
          Args:
              max_entries: Upper limit on the number of entries stored in the ring buffer.
                          Newer entries replace older ones when the buffer is full.
              isolated: When True, initializes a standalone FlightRecorder instance
                       for this hook rather than referencing the global singleton.
          )",
          py::arg("max_entries") = 2048,
          py::arg("isolated") = false)
      .def(
          "register_with_comm",
          &FlightRecorderHook::registerWithComm,
          R"(
          Attach this hook to a TorchComm communicator.
          Args:
              comm: The target communicator to attach to.
          )",
          py::arg("comm"),
          py::call_guard<py::gil_scoped_release>())
      .def(
          "unregister",
          &FlightRecorderHook::unregister,
          "Detach this hook from all associated communicators.",
          py::call_guard<py::gil_scoped_release>())
      .def(
          "dump_json",
          &FlightRecorderHook::dump_json,
          R"(
          Export all recorded entries as a JSON string conforming to the OSS FlightRecorder schema.
          This output is compatible with the fr_trace diagnostic utilities provided by
          torch.distributed.flight_recorder.
          Args:
              include_completed: If False, only return incomplete (active) entries.
          Returns:
              A JSON-formatted string representing the flight recorder trace.
          )",
          py::arg("include_completed") = true,
          py::call_guard<py::gil_scoped_release>())
      .def(
          "reset",
          &FlightRecorderHook::reset,
          "Erase all stored entries and reset internal sequence counters.",
          py::call_guard<py::gil_scoped_release>())
      .def(
          "is_enabled",
          &FlightRecorderHook::isEnabled,
          "Determine whether any communicators are currently registered.")
      .def(
          "__len__",
          &FlightRecorderHook::size,
          "Retrieve the current count of stored entries.")
      .def(
          "count",
          &FlightRecorderHook::size,
          "Retrieve the current count of stored entries.")
      .def(
          "dump_file",
          &FlightRecorderHook::dump_file,
          R"(
          Export the flight recorder trace to a file on disk.
          The destination path is governed by the TORCHCOMM_FR_DUMP_TEMP_FILE
          environment variable. Files follow the naming pattern <prefix><rank>.
          Args:
              rank: Identifier used in the filename.
              include_completed: If False, only write incomplete entries.
          )",
          py::arg("rank"),
          py::arg("include_completed") = true,
          py::call_guard<py::gil_scoped_release>());
}

//-*****************************************************************************
void register_filmbackxformop()
{
    // FilmBackXformOp
    //
    class_<AbcG::FilmBackXformOp>(
          "FilmBackXformOp",
          "This class stores information regarding a specific transformation operation, "
          "without containing the actual data needed to compute a 3x3 matrix. It specifies "
          "the operation type (Translate, Scale, Matrix), an optional hint for applications "
          "like Maya, and indicates which aspects of the operation may vary over time.",
         init<const AbcG::FilmBackXformOperationType, const std::string&>(
             ( arg( "operation_type" ), arg( "application_hint" ) = 0 ),
             "Construct a FilmBackXformOp using default settings derived from the operation type "
             "and an application-specific hint." ) )
        .def( init<>("Initialize an empty FilmBackXformOp instance" ) )
        .def( "getOperationType",
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getType,
              "Retrieve the kind of transformation performed. (Translate, Scale, Matrix)")
        .def( "getApplicationHint",
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getHint,
              "Retrieve the hint used to distinguish between variations that share the same type.")
        .def( "getFullTypeHint",
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getHint,
              "Obtain both the type and hint as a string, where the first character denotes "
              "the operation (t for translate, s for scale, m for matrix) and subsequent "
              "characters represent the optional hint." )
        .def( "getChannelCount",
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getNumChannels,
              "Determine how many components this operation contains based on its type. "
              "Translate and Scale each use 2 channels, while Matrix uses 9." )
        .def( "getValueAt", 
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getChannelValue,
              ( arg( "channel_index" ) ),
              "Fetch the value at a specific channel; returns 0 if the index exceeds"
              "the valid range." )
        .def( "setValueAt",
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::setChannelValue,
              ( arg( "channel_index" ), arg( "new_value" ) ),
              "Assign a new value to a specific channel; no change occurs if the index is out of bounds.")
        .def( "applyTranslation", 
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::setTranslate,
              ( arg( "translation_vector" ) ) )
        .def( "applyScaling", 
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::setScale,
              ( arg( "scale_vector" ) ) )
        .def( "applyTransformationMatrix", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::setMatrix,
              ( arg( "transformation_matrix" ) ) )
        .def( "extractTranslation", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getTranslate )
        .def( "extractScale", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getScale )
        .def( "extractMatrix", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getMatrix )
        .def( "isTranslationOperation", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::isTranslateOp )
        .def( "isScalingOperation", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::isScaleOp )
        .def( "isMatrixOperation", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::isMatrixOp )
        ;
}

// Custom type trait to check if T is convertible to any integer type (excluding character and boolean types)
template <typename T>
struct is_integer_convertible : boost::mpl::and_<
    // Exclude boolean and all character types
    boost::mpl::not_<std::is_same<T, bool>>,
    boost::mpl::not_<std::is_same<T, char>>,
    boost::mpl::not_<std::is_same<T, unsigned char>>,
    boost::mpl::not_<std::is_same<T, signed char>>,
    boost::mpl::not_<std::is_same<T, wchar_t>>,
    boost::mpl::not_<std::is_same<T, char16_t>>,
    boost::mpl::not_<std::is_same<T, char32_t>>,
    
    // Check if T can be converted to any of the standard integer types
    boost::mpl::or_<
        boost::is_convertible<T, int>,
        boost::is_convertible<T, unsigned int>,
        boost::is_convertible<T, long>,
        boost::is_convertible<T, unsigned long>,
        boost::is_convertible<T, long long>,
        boost::is_convertible<T, unsigned long long>,
        boost::is_convertible<T, short>,
        boost::is_convertible<T, unsigned short>
    >
> {};

struct FToolCommandDef
{
    TSharedPtr<FAutoRegisterUICommand> CommandPtr;
    FName CommandName;
    FText Label;
    FText Tooltip;
    EUserInterfaceActionType ActionType;
    FInputChord InputChord;

    FToolCommandDef(FName InName, const FText& InLabel, const FText& InTooltip,
                    EUserInterfaceActionType InType, const FInputChord& InChord)
        : CommandPtr(nullptr)
        , CommandName(InName)
        , Label(InLabel)
        , Tooltip(InTooltip)
        , ActionType(InType)
        , InputChord(InChord)
    {}
};

namespace py = pybind11;
using namespace torch::comms::fr;

PYBIND11_MODULE(_fr, m) {
  // Bind FlightRecorderHook class
  py::class_<FlightRecorderHook, std::shared_ptr<FlightRecorderHook>>(
      m,
      "FlightRecorderHook",
      R"(
FlightRecorderHook monitors all collective operations in flight for TorchComm communicators.
The output format aligns with the OSS FlightRecorder format from PyTorch's
distributed module, enabling trace analysis using the same fr_trace tools.
Example:
    >>> from torchcomms.hooks import fr
    >>> comm = torchcomms.new_comm("nccl", device, "world")
    >>> monitor = fr.FlightRecorderHook(max_capacity=1024)
    >>> monitor.bind_to_comm(comm)
    >>> # ... execute some collectives ...
    >>> json_output = monitor.export_json()
For testing, use ``isolated=True`` to instantiate a dedicated FlightRecorder instance
that remains independent from other hooks::
    >>> monitor = fr.FlightRecorderHook(max_capacity=100, isolated=True)
      )")
      .def(
          py::init<size_t, bool>(),
          R"(
          Construct a FlightRecorderHook with configurable buffer capacity.
          Args:
              max_capacity: Upper limit on the number of entries stored in the ring buffer.
                           Newer entries replace older ones once the buffer is full.
              isolated: When True, initializes an independent FlightRecorder instance
                       specifically for this hook rather than referencing the global singleton.
          )",
          py::arg("max_capacity") = 2048,
          py::arg("isolated") = false)
      .def(
          "bind_to_comm",
          &FlightRecorderHook::registerWithComm,
          R"(
          Link this hook to a TorchComm communicator.
          Args:
              comm: The communicator to associate with.
          )",
          py::arg("comm"),
          py::call_guard<py::gil_scoped_release>())
      .def(
          "detach",
          &FlightRecorderHook::unregister,
          "Remove this hook from all associated communicators.",
          py::call_guard<py::gil_scoped_release>())
      .def(
          "export_json",
          &FlightRecorderHook::dump_json,
          R"(
          Export all recorded entries as a JSON string conforming to the OSS FlightRecorder schema.
          This structure is compatible with the fr_trace diagnostic utilities provided by
          torch.distributed.flight_recorder.
          Args:
              include_completed: If set to False, only include entries still in progress.
          Returns:
              A JSON-formatted string representing the flight recorder data.
          )",
          py::arg("include_completed") = true,
          py::call_guard<py::gil_scoped_release>())
      .def(
          "clear",
          &FlightRecorderHook::reset,
          "Erase all stored entries and reinitialize sequence counters.",
          py::call_guard<py::gil_scoped_release>())
      .def(
          "is_active",
          &FlightRecorderHook::isEnabled,
          "Determine whether the hook has any registered communicators.")
      .def(
          "__len__",
          &FlightRecorderHook::size,
          "Retrieve the current count of stored entries.")
      .def(
          "count",
          &FlightRecorderHook::size,
          "Retrieve the current count of stored entries.")
      .def(
          "write_to_file",
          &FlightRecorderHook::dump_file,
          R"(
          Export the flight recorder trace and save it to disk.
          The destination path is governed by the TORCHCOMM_FR_DUMP_TEMP_FILE
          environment variable. Files are generated as <prefix><rank>.
          Args:
              rank: Identifier used in constructing the filename.
              include_completed: If False, only write entries that remain incomplete.
          )",
          py::arg("rank"),
          py::arg("include_completed") = true,
          py::call_guard<py::gil_scoped_release>());
}

void register_filmbackxformop()
{
    // FilmBackXformOp
    //
    class_<AbcG::FilmBackXformOp>(
          "FilmBackXformOp",
          "This class stores information about a specific transformation operation, "
          "without containing the actual data needed to compute a 3x3 matrix. "
          "It records the operation type (Translate, Scale, Matrix), an optional "
          "application-specific hint (e.g., for Maya), and flags indicating which "
          "aspects may vary over time.",
         init<const AbcG::FilmBackXformOperationType, const std::string&>(
             ( arg( "operation_type" ), arg( "application_hint" ) = "" ),
             "Constructs a FilmBackXformOp initialized with the given operation type "
             "and optional application-specific hint." ) )
        .def( init<>("Default constructor creates an empty FilmBackXformOp instance" ) )
        .def( "getOperationType",
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getType,
              "Returns the kind of transform this object represents: "
              "translation, scaling, or matrix-based." )
        .def( "getApplicationHint",
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getHint,
              "Returns the application-specific hint string used for "
              "disambiguating similar operation types across different DCC tools." )
        .def( "getFullTypeHint",
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getHint,
              "Returns a combined string where the first character indicates "
              "the operation type ('t', 's', or 'm') followed by the optional hint." )
        .def( "componentCount",
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getNumChannels,
              "Returns how many scalar values are involved in this operation: "
              "2 for translate/scale, 9 for matrix." )
        .def( "getValueAt",
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getChannelValue,
              ( arg( "channel_index" ) ),
              "Retrieves the value at the specified channel index; returns 0 if out of range." )
        .def( "setValueAt",
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::setChannelValue,
              ( arg( "channel_index" ), arg( "new_value" ) ),
              "Assigns a new value to the given channel; no effect if index is invalid." )
        .def( "assignTranslation", 
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::setTranslate,
              ( arg( "translation_vector" ) ) )
        .def( "assignScaling", 
              &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::setScale,
              ( arg( "scale_vector" ) ) )
        .def( "assignMatrix", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::setMatrix,
              ( arg( "transformation_matrix" ) ) )
        .def( "extractTranslation", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getTranslate )
        .def( "extractScale", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getScale )
        .def( "extractMatrix", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::getMatrix )
        .def( "isTranslationOnly", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::isTranslateOp )
        .def( "isScalingOnly", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::isScaleOp )
        .def( "isMatrixOnly", &AbcG::FilmBackXformOp::isMatrixOp )
        ;
}
